questions.question: Explain the difference between (−3)^2 and −3^2 and give the value of each.
questions.expected_answer: In (−3)^2 the brackets make −3 the base, so (−3)(−3) = 9. In −3^2 the base is 3; square it to get 9 and then apply the negative sign: −9.

questions.question: Why is a negative base with an even exponent always positive?
questions.expected_answer: The negative factors pair off, and each pair of negatives multiplies to a positive. With an even exponent every factor is in a pair, so the product is positive; with an odd exponent one negative is left over.

questions.question: Write 3 × 3 × 5 × 5 × 5 in exponential form and explain why 15^5 is wrong.
questions.expected_answer: 3^2 × 5^3. Exponents count identical factors, so the two threes and three fives are counted separately. 15^5 would mean five factors of fifteen, which is 759 375, far larger than 1 125.
